decisions.claim_text_original: The accepted scientific name is Monstera deliciosa Liebm.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Nom accepté : Monstera deliciosa Liebm.
decisions.rationale: POWO directly records the species as accepted; IPNI independently confirms the nomenclatural name, authorship and original publication. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa belongs to genus Monstera, family Araceae, order Alismatales.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Araceae · Monstera · Alismatales.
decisions.rationale: Direct POWO classification; IPNI confirms family as entered. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera borsigiana K.Koch is treated by POWO as a synonym of Monstera deliciosa, not as a separate accepted species.
prohibited_wording: Monstera borsigiana est une espèce acceptée distincte
decisions.candidate_public_wording: « Monstera borsigiana » est aujourd'hui traité par POWO comme un synonyme de Monstera deliciosa, et non comme une espèce distincte.
decisions.rationale: Direct synonymy entry in the authoritative taxonomic backbone. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Philodendron pertusum is listed by POWO among the synonyms of Monstera deliciosa.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Philodendron pertusum est un nom historique placé en synonymie, pas le nom accepté actuel.
decisions.rationale: Direct POWO synonymy record. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: POWO records the native range as southern Mexico (Veracruz, Oaxaca and Chiapas) to Guatemala.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Aire native documentée par POWO : sud du Mexique — notamment Veracruz, Oaxaca et Chiapas — jusqu'au Guatemala.
decisions.rationale: Direct native-range record from POWO. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa primarily grows in the wet tropical biome.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Biome principal : tropical humide.
decisions.rationale: Direct POWO biome field. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa is a climbing liana that uses supports in forest habitats.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: C'est une liane grimpante : dans son milieu, elle progresse en s'appuyant sur des supports végétaux.
decisions.rationale: POWO identifies a liana; RHS, NC State and UF/IFAS independently describe climbing habit/support use. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera is described in botanical literature as a secondary hemiepiphytic climbing lineage; applying that label to M. deliciosa is supported but should retain context.
decisions.required_qualifier: Muir and Croat support the life form mainly at genus level; NC State describes the species starting terrestrially then becoming epiphytic upon reaching a support.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Son développement est souvent décrit comme secondairement hémiépiphyte : elle débute au sol puis grimpe sur un support, tout en conservant une relation avec le sol selon son stade et son milieu.
decisions.rationale: Muir and Croat support the life form mainly at genus level; NC State describes the species starting terrestrially then becoming epiphytic upon reaching a support. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera exhibits marked ontogenetic changes in leaf form (heteroblasty), with juvenile and mature leaves differing substantially.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: La forme des feuilles change avec le développement : les feuilles juvéniles et adultes ne présentent pas la même découpe.
decisions.rationale: Croat and Muir explicitly discuss heteroblasty in Monstera; NC State independently distinguishes mature perforated leaves. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Mature Monstera deliciosa leaves can develop both margin-reaching divisions and internal perforations.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: À maturité, les feuilles peuvent présenter à la fois des découpes atteignant le bord et des perforations internes.
decisions.rationale: Specific descriptions from NC State and UF/IFAS converge; Muir treats adult fenestration as the defining trait under study. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: The adaptive function of Monstera leaf fenestration is not established as a single proven fact; Muir proposes a model-based growth-variance hypothesis for patchy understory light.
decisions.required_qualifier: Peer-reviewed modeling paper explicitly frames the result as a testable hypothesis and reviews competing conjectures.
prohibited_wording: les fenestrations servent certainement à laisser passer la lumière
decisions.candidate_public_wording: La fonction évolutive des fenestrations n'est pas démontrée par une explication unique. Une hypothèse scientifique propose qu'elles répartissent mieux la lumière intermittente du sous-bois, mais elle reste à tester.
decisions.rationale: Peer-reviewed modeling paper explicitly frames the result as a testable hypothesis and reviews competing conjectures. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Maturity is clearly associated with fenestration; brighter filtered light and climbing support are horticulturally associated with more mature leaf form, but neither should be presented as a guaranteed single trigger.
decisions.required_qualifier: Maturity is corroborated by morphology sources; RHS and UConn give horticultural associations for light/support without controlled causal proof.
prohibited_wording: un tuteur fera apparaître les trous
decisions.candidate_public_wording: L'absence de fenestrations est d'abord compatible avec un stade juvénile. Une lumière filtrée suffisante et un support adapté favorisent une croissance plus mature, sans garantir à eux seuls l'apparition de découpes.
decisions.rationale: Maturity is corroborated by morphology sources; RHS and UConn give horticultural associations for light/support without controlled causal proof. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: For indoor cultivation, bright or moderate indirect/filtered light is consistently recommended; strong direct sun can scorch leaves.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Placez-la dans une lumière lumineuse à modérée, filtrée ou indirecte. Un soleil direct intense peut brûler le feuillage ; toute exposition plus forte demande une acclimatation progressive.
decisions.rationale: RHS profile/guide and NC State independently converge; UConn's regional partial-sun guidance reinforces the need for acclimation/context rather than a universal direct-sun prohibition. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Water thoroughly after the upper portion of the potting medium has dried appreciably; do not use a fixed calendar interval.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Contrôlez le substrat plutôt que le calendrier : laissez sa partie supérieure sécher nettement, puis arrosez à fond et laissez l'excédent s'écouler.
decisions.rationale: RHS says allow compost to become almost dry; NC State specifies the upper quarter to third; UConn gives 2–3 inches. They converge on substrate state but differ in operational threshold. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Prolonged saturation or standing water increases the risk of root and stem rot.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Ne laissez pas le pot baigner durablement dans l'eau : un milieu constamment saturé augmente le risque de pourriture racinaire.
decisions.rationale: RHS and UConn independently connect persistent wetness/standing water with rot risk. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa prefers moderate-to-high or humid air, but the evidence reviewed does not establish a universal required relative-humidity range.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Elle apprécie un air modérément à assez humide, mais ce n'est pas une raison pour présenter une plage universelle obligatoire.
decisions.rationale: RHS and NC State independently state a qualitative preference; no opened authoritative source validates the historical 50–75% band as a species requirement. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: The historical Jungle range 50–75% RH is not sufficiently supported as a universal Monstera deliciosa requirement.
decisions.rationale: Opened institutional sources use qualitative terms; none supports both bounds in the same context. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.
decisions.open_question: Nouvelle preuve ou décision explicitement prévue par le pack requise avant réexamen.

decisions.claim_text_original: Institutional indoor guidance consistently favors warm conditions, but exact bands vary: RHS gives 18–25°C while NC State gives 60–85°F (about 15.6–29.4°C).
decisions.required_qualifier: Reliable sources converge qualitatively but not on identical numeric bounds.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Conservez-la au chaud et à l'écart des courants d'air froids. Les guides institutionnels consultés donnent des plages différentes selon leur contexte ; évitez d'en faire une limite universelle.
decisions.rationale: Reliable sources converge qualitatively but not on identical numeric bounds. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: A universal minimum of 15°C is not established by the reviewed evidence; sources distinguish preferred indoor warmth, outdoor handling and cold-damage thresholds.
decisions.rationale: NC State's lower preferred bound approximates 15.6°C, RHS gives 18°C or 18–25°C, UConn uses 45°F/7.2°C for summer outdoor handling, and UF/IFAS gives freeze-damage thresholds; these are not equivalent endpoints. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.
decisions.open_question: Nouvelle preuve ou décision explicitement prévue par le pack requise avant réexamen.

decisions.claim_text_original: Container media should be open/aerated, well drained and retain some organic matter/moisture without remaining saturated.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Visez un substrat ouvert, aéré et drainant, contenant de la matière organique mais ne restant pas saturé.
decisions.rationale: RHS and UConn converge on open/well-drained and organic-rich media; rot guidance supports avoiding persistent saturation. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Use a container that permits drainage and increase size incrementally rather than overpotting.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Choisissez un contenant drainant, seulement un peu plus grand que la motte ; un pot surdimensionné reste humide plus longtemps.
decisions.rationale: RHS and UConn independently warn against disproportionate container size and persistent wetness. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Repotting is justified by rootball/container fit and stability, not a rigid annual schedule; roots reaching the pot's bottom and sides are a direct check.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Rempotez lorsque les racines occupent réellement le contenant — notamment lorsqu'elles atteignent le fond et les côtés — ou lorsque la stabilité devient insuffisante, plutôt que selon un calendrier rigide.
decisions.rationale: UConn gives a direct root inspection criterion; RHS discusses rootball fit and top-heaviness while providing only a broad timing tendency. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Balanced fertiliser is recommended during active growth; exact frequency differs among institutional sources.
decisions.required_qualifier: RHS guide/profile converge on balanced feed in growth, with one specifying monthly; UConn cautions about salts and gives regional active-growth months.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Fertilisez modérément pendant la croissance active avec un engrais équilibré, en suivant le dosage du produit et en évitant l'accumulation de sels. La fréquence dépend du produit et des conditions réelles.
decisions.rationale: RHS guide/profile converge on balanced feed in growth, with one specifying monthly; UConn cautions about salts and gives regional active-growth months. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Vegetative propagation by stem cutting requires stem tissue containing at least one node; a detached leaf without a node is not supported as a method for producing a complete new plant.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Pour obtenir une nouvelle plante par bouture de tige, conservez au moins un nœud. Une feuille isolée sans nœud ne constitue pas une bouture de tige viable pour reformer une plante complète.
decisions.rationale: UConn's species-specific cutting instruction locates the cut below a node; Iowa State's protocol requires nodes and explicitly lists M. deliciosa as suitable for stem cuttings. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: A support helps manage the natural climbing habit and physical stability; associations with larger, more mature leaves are documented horticulturally but are not a guaranteed fenestration switch.
decisions.required_qualifier: NC State directly supports physical stability; RHS and UConn associate climbing with mature/larger leaves; controlled causality is not established.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Un support accompagne son port grimpant et stabilise les tiges. Il peut favoriser l'expression d'une croissance plus mature, sans garantir à lui seul de grandes feuilles ou des fenestrations.
decisions.rationale: NC State directly supports physical stability; RHS and UConn associate climbing with mature/larger leaves; controlled causality is not established. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Aerial roots arise from vine nodes and contribute to anchorage/climbing; they may continue growing and can root on contacting suitable ground or substrate.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Les racines aériennes participent à l'ancrage et à la progression de la liane ; au contact d'un milieu favorable, certaines peuvent s'y enraciner.
decisions.rationale: UF/IFAS specifically describes emergence and rooting on ground contact; RHS describes rooting into a moist support; peer-reviewed work confirms distinct aerial-root growth/anatomy. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: The reviewed direct evidence is insufficient to issue a universal rule that aerial roots should always be cut, never cut, or always guided into the pot.
decisions.rationale: Opened sources document role/anatomy but not a controlled universal home-practice rule. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.
decisions.open_question: Nouvelle preuve ou décision explicitement prévue par le pack requise avant réexamen.

decisions.claim_text_original: Reported dimensions depend strongly on context: outdoor/wild-like vines may exceed 21 m in length, RHS gives 4–8 m under its horticultural profile, and NC State gives about 1.8–2.4 m in most home environments.
decisions.required_qualifier: Institutional sources directly give values but for non-equivalent settings.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: La liane peut dépasser 20 m dans des conditions extérieures favorables ; en intérieur, elle reste généralement bien plus contenue, souvent autour de quelques mètres selon l'espace, le support et la taille.
decisions.rationale: Institutional sources directly give values but for non-equivalent settings. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa is described as vigorous or fast growing in favorable horticultural/outdoor contexts, but no universal indoor growth rate is established.
decisions.required_qualifier: RHS describes vigorous plants and UF/IFAS fast outdoor vine growth; neither defines a transferable indoor rate.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Sa croissance peut être vigoureuse lorsque les conditions sont favorables, mais sa vitesse réelle en intérieur varie fortement avec la lumière, la chaleur, l'espace racinaire et le support.
decisions.rationale: RHS describes vigorous plants and UF/IFAS fast outdoor vine growth; neither defines a transferable indoor rate. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Monstera deliciosa contains insoluble needle-like calcium oxalate crystals associated with oral and contact irritation.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: La plante contient des cristaux insolubles d'oxalate de calcium pouvant irriter la bouche, les muqueuses et, chez certaines personnes, la peau.
decisions.rationale: ASPCA directly identifies insoluble calcium oxalates in the species; NC State independently identifies needle-like calcium oxalate crystals and contact dermatitis. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Chewing oxalate-containing plant tissue can cause acute oral pain, irritation, swelling and difficulty swallowing; keep Monstera deliciosa out of children's reach and seek professional poison-control/medical advice for concerning exposure.
decisions.required_qualifier: NC State is species-specific; CHOP provides direct institutional mechanism and symptom guidance for oxalate plants generally; RHS advises keeping the species away from children.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Gardez la plante hors de portée des enfants. En cas de mastication ou d'irritation importante — notamment gonflement ou difficulté à avaler — contactez un centre antipoison ou un professionnel de santé.
decisions.rationale: NC State is species-specific; CHOP provides direct institutional mechanism and symptom guidance for oxalate plants generally; RHS advises keeping the species away from children. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: ASPCA classifies Monstera deliciosa as toxic to dogs and cats; chewing can cause oral irritation, drooling, vomiting and difficulty swallowing.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Toxique pour les chiens et les chats en cas de mastication. Une irritation buccale, une salivation excessive, des vomissements ou une difficulté à avaler peuvent survenir ; contactez un vétérinaire ou un centre antipoison vétérinaire si une exposition est suspectée.
decisions.rationale: Direct species-specific ASPCA Animal Poison Control profile. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Scale insects and spider mites are directly documented for Monstera deliciosa; UConn additionally documents mealybugs and aphids. Thrips are plausible houseplant pests but were not directly documented for this species in the opened species-specific sources.
decisions.required_qualifier: RHS/UConn provide species-specific pest records; the opened thrips source is general-domain only.
prohibited_wording: thrips établi spécifiquement pour Monstera deliciosa
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Surveillez surtout les cochenilles et les acariens, directement documentés sur cette espèce. Les cochenilles farineuses sont également signalées. Les thrips restent une hypothèse à confirmer par inspection, pas un diagnostic automatique.
decisions.rationale: RHS/UConn provide species-specific pest records; the opened thrips source is general-domain only. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Fine stippling, bronzing/bleaching and webbing are compatible with spider mites; inspect leaf undersides with magnification or tap over white paper.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: De fines ponctuations claires et des toiles peuvent évoquer des acariens. Vérifiez le revers des feuilles à la loupe ou secouez une feuille au-dessus d'un papier blanc avant d'agir.
decisions.rationale: UConn gives species-specific signs; UMN provides independent diagnostic procedure for twospotted mites. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Yellow leaves are non-specific. Possible causes include root-zone saturation/rot, pest feeding, disease, cold or natural leaf senescence; diagnosis requires checking substrate, roots, temperature history and pests.
decisions.required_qualifier: UConn directly documents yellowing from scale/mealybugs and root/stem rot signs; RHS supports wet-root risk. Natural senescence is general plant biology but was not found in a species-specific source during this pilot.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Une feuille jaune ne suffit pas à conclure. Contrôlez d'abord l'humidité du substrat, l'état des racines, les températures récentes et la présence de ravageurs ; une vieille feuille isolée peut aussi simplement terminer son cycle.
decisions.rationale: UConn directly documents yellowing from scale/mealybugs and root/stem rot signs; RHS supports wet-root risk. Natural senescence is general plant biology but was not found in a species-specific source during this pilot. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Brown edges or patches are non-specific; dry air or direct-sun scorch are supported possibilities, while patterned lesions, yellow margins or ooze require disease assessment.
decisions.required_qualifier: RHS links dry air and direct sun to browning/scorch; UConn describes bacterial/anthracnose lesion patterns.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Des bords bruns peuvent être compatibles avec un air très sec ou une brûlure lumineuse. Si les taches s'étendent, présentent un halo jaune ou un suintement, isolez la plante et faites préciser le diagnostic.
decisions.rationale: RHS links dry air and direct sun to browning/scorch; UConn describes bacterial/anthracnose lesion patterns. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Slow growth or smaller leaves may reflect low light, seasonal/temperature context, root-zone constraint or a return to less mature growth after pruning; support is an association, not a guaranteed cure.
decisions.required_qualifier: RHS links low light and post-pruning growth to less mature leaves; UConn links support attachment with leaf-size increase; root constraints and temperature need contextual inspection.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Une croissance ralentie ou de petites feuilles demandent de vérifier ensemble la lumière, la saison, la température, l'espace racinaire et le port de la plante. Un support peut accompagner la maturité, mais ne constitue pas une correction garantie.
decisions.rationale: RHS links low light and post-pruning growth to less mature leaves; UConn links support attachment with leaf-size increase; root constraints and temperature need contextual inspection. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Lack of fenestrations is compatible with juvenile stage and can also be associated with insufficient light or non-climbing growth; it is not evidence of a single fault.
decisions.required_qualifier: Stage is corroborated; light/support associations come from institutional horticultural guidance.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Des feuilles sans fenestrations peuvent être normales sur une plante jeune. Vérifiez aussi si la lumière est suffisante et si la liane peut grimper, sans promettre qu'un tuteur fera apparaître les découpes.
decisions.rationale: Stage is corroborated; light/support associations come from institutional horticultural guidance. Publication Evidence V1: REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decisions.claim_text_original: Stems can be pruned to control size; pruning may be followed by smaller, less mature leaves during regrowth.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Vous pouvez raccourcir les tiges pour contenir la plante. La repousse peut d'abord produire des feuilles plus petites et moins matures.
decisions.rationale: RHS and UF/IFAS independently support stem pruning for size; RHS supplies the regrowth qualifier. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: Wiping accumulated dust from leaves is recommended as routine care and also provides an opportunity to inspect for pests.
decisions.candidate_public_wording: Essuyez doucement la poussière avec un support propre et profitez-en pour examiner le revers des feuilles. Aucun produit lustrant n'est nécessaire.
decisions.rationale: RHS recommends regular wiping for dust/insect inspection; NC State independently recommends wiping dust from leaves. Publication Evidence V1: DRAFT.

decisions.claim_text_original: The Jungle light score 4/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
decisions.rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.

decisions.claim_text_original: The Jungle watering score 2/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
decisions.rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.

decisions.claim_text_original: The Jungle humidity score 3/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
decisions.rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.

decisions.rationale: No explicit documented scoring criteria have been applied. Publication Evidence V1: WITHHELD.

decisions.claim_text_original: Evidence exists to answer placement, watering trigger, lack of fenestrations, repotting trigger, drained-container and toxicity questions cautiously; universal aerial-root cutting guidance remains unsupported.
decisions.required_qualifier: This is a coverage assessment derived from the atomic claims, not a final FAQ.
